title: Rodent baiting and bait boxes
subtitle: Based on Mitch's answers and the product labels, checked against NSW requirements. Updated 6 Nov 2026.
source: Mitch's answers 6 Nov 2026; LPC Tech Onboarding Pack (PPE, never list, what you can quote); jobbook-data/chemicals.json and the SDS files (Rodent Treatment and Rodent Boxes products); jobbook-data/services.json (past wordings); business-context notes (quarterly default, external boxes)

sections.heading: When this job comes up
body: Rodent baiting, bait station checks and bait box cleaning. Mitch's services are Rodent Treatment and Rodent Boxes (supply). Past invoices read: "Inspect, clean and refill rodent bait boxes", "Rodent Baiting", "Rodent Baiting to ceiling" and "Supply refillable tamperproof rodent bait boxes".

Rodent baiting usually comes back every quarter. That is Mitch's default, and he can change it for a client. Second-generation baits (see the Law box) must be checked at least every 35 days while they are out, so quarterly is not enough for them. Do not leave one in place for longer without ringing Mitch.
We use bait only. No traps.
Once you are experienced you can quote a bait box refill. Anything complex goes to Mitch. Commercial rodent jobs do not all go to Mitch, they can be shared around.
The job process, the never list, PPE and the free service period are in the Every job guide.

sections.heading: What the law and the label require

items.text: Follow the product label
items.detail: Using a pesticide against its label is an offence. If the job needs something the label does not allow, stop and call Mitch.

items.text: Make the record the same day
items.detail: Every pesticide job needs a record: full product name, date, target pest, rate and quantity, address and area treated, who applied it, equipment, and start and finish times. It must be made within 48 hours and kept at least 3 years. Give the customer a copy if they ask.

items.text: Only do work your licence covers
items.detail: If a treatment is outside your licence class, work under Mitch's direct supervision and do not do it alone.

items.text: Protect people, pets and the environment
items.detail: Wear the PPE the label and SDS call for. Keep spray and bait away from people, pets, food, drains and waterways. Harming people, wildlife or property with a pesticide is an offence.

items.text: Second-generation baits: Talon GT Pro, Talon XT Pro, Roban, Generation First Strike
items.detail: These contain brodifacoum, difenacoum or difethialone. APVMA conditions of use apply from March 2026. Use them only as the APVMA instructions say, and give the customer the printed instructions. Never: outdoor mouse baiting, burrow baiting, or loose bait where pets, children or other animals can reach it. Outdoors: tamper-resistant, weather-resistant station, fixed in place, no more than 2 m from a building. Check the infestation and results at least every 35 days of continuous use. At every visit: search for dead rodents and dispose of them, gloves on. Selontra and Fastrac are not second-generation baits, so these conditions are not about them. Follow their labels.

items.text: Roof voids and subfloors: asbestos
items.detail: Houses built before 1990 can have asbestos (roof insulation, eaves, cladding). Do not disturb anything that might be asbestos. Stop and tell Mitch.

items.text: Roof voids: live wiring
items.detail: Look first. Do not touch cables. If you are not sure it is safe, do not go in and tell Mitch.

items.text: Tight or stuffy spaces
items.detail: If you cannot get out easily, or the air feels wrong, do not go in. Tell Mitch first.

sections.heading: PPE
sections.title: PPE on before you go in
sections.note: Never apply chemicals without PPE. If the SDS requires it, you wear it. No exceptions.
items: Gloves and closed shoes at minimum

items.text: Gloves at all times when handling traps or bait
items.detail: Wear them every time you touch a bait box or any bait.

items.text: Roof void entry: dust mask, gloves, torch, appropriate footwear
Subfloor entry: coveralls, gloves, dust mask, torch

sections.heading: Where the boxes go

items.text: Outside: tamper-resistant boxes, always
items.detail: Attached to the wall, fixed in place, no more than 2 m from the building. Existing boxes are re-used if they are safe and tamper-resistant.

items.text: Inside: you can bait inside too
items.detail: Use a tamper-resistant box anywhere kids, pets or other animals can reach. Check what the client is happy with.

items.text: Replace a box when it is unsafe

items: How many boxes on a standard house, and how far apart: Mitch sets this for each job. Ask him until you are doing it on your own.

sections.heading: Steps
sections.title: Steps
items: Ask the customer where they have seen or heard rodents
Gloves on before you touch a bait box or any bait

items.text: Inspect each bait box
items.detail: Is it attached and safe? A box that is unsafe gets replaced. Record how much bait was taken: none, some or all.

items.text: Clean each bait box
items.detail: Gloves on. Bag the old bait and anything you wipe out of the box, and take it back to Mitch.

items.text: Refill each bait box with fresh bait
items.detail: Old bait goes off and is less attractive to rodents, so it is usually replaced, whether the box was eaten out or not touched. Apply per the product label. Never exceed label rates.

items.text: Old or mouldy bait: bag it or box it, take it back and give it to Mitch
Bait the ceiling void or cavity when the job includes it
items.detail: Roof void entry PPE applies. Second-generation bait goes only in a tamper-resistant station or where pets, children and other animals (such as possums) cannot reach. If you are not sure, ring Mitch. Mitch will show you where in the void on the ride-along.

items.text: Look for dead rodents at every visit and take away the ones you can find, gloves on
items.detail: The APVMA instructions for second-generation baits require it. If you cannot reach one, tell Mitch.

items.text: Second-generation bait: check how long it has been out
items.detail: Never more than 35 days of continuous use without checking the infestation and results. Book the next check inside that.

items.text: Second-generation bait: give the customer the printed APVMA instructions

items: Keep chemicals away from food, children and pets

items.text: Tell the customer about food storage
items.detail: We do not really look at how they are getting in. Sealing gaps is a job for a builder or chippy. If you can see an obvious gap, you can say so.

items: Take BEFORE and AFTER photos, and photograph any rodent evidence or damage you find
Note anything you could not treat or reach, and why

sections.heading: Job complete when
items: Every bait box on the property inspected, cleaned and refilled, or noted with the reason it was not
Bait taken recorded for each box (none, some or all)
Old or mouldy bait bagged or boxed to take back to Mitch
Anything you could not treat or reach is noted on the job report, with the reason
Product, rate, area and quantity recorded on the job report
Customer told what you did, and about food storage
Customer told when to expect the next baiting visit (within 35 days if second-generation bait is out)
Printed APVMA instructions given to the customer, if you used second-generation bait
Service report left, or customer told it is being emailed

items.q: Will the bait get rid of them?
items.a: They eat the bait, then go looking for water, and most of the time they leave. There are no guarantees.

items.q: How long does the bait last?
items.a: As long as it lasts. It depends on how many rodents there are, which is the rodent pressure.

items.q: Is the bait safe for my kids and pets?
items.a: Wherever kids, pets or other animals could reach it, the bait goes in a tamper-resistant box. Outside the boxes are fixed to the wall. We check you are happy with where they go.

items.q: Will you take away any dead rodents?
items.a: We look for them at every visit and take away the ones we can find. If one is out of reach, we will tell you so you can arrange it.
That is more a job for a builder or chippy. If we can see an obvious gap, we will say so. Keep food stored away too.

sections.heading: Tell Mitch straight away if
sections.body: Call Mitch on 0432 181 689. After hours or urgent, call Mitch directly.

items.text: You apply the wrong chemical
items.detail: Stop immediately. Do not continue. Call Mitch.

items.text: There is a spill
items.detail: Follow the SDS procedure. Call Mitch immediately. Never leave a spill unattended.

items.text: Someone is hurt
items.detail: Treat the injury first. Call Mitch. Write down what happened.

items.text: The customer complains or gets aggressive
items.detail: Stay calm and do not argue. For a complaint, tell them Mitch will call them today. If they are aggressive, remove yourself. Call Mitch either way.

items.text: The customer asks for a quote on anything complex, or you are not sure
items.detail: Say "I'll need to get Mitch to come and have a look and provide a quote for that."

items.text: You see signs of termites or other pests outside this job
items.detail: Photograph it and tell Mitch. Termite quotes always go to Mitch.

Law and safety points checked on 6 Nov 2026 against the NSW Pesticides Regulation 2017 (clauses 35 to 37 on records and 13 to 16 on supervision, as published by the NSW EPA) and SafeWork NSW pages, and the APVMA notice on rodent baits (Gazette No 5, 10 March 2026). Changes to the Regulation since 2017 were not checked.
